chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), 'May I be your sacrifice! You granted us understanding in the religion, and God made us needless of [other] people through you, to the extent that a group from us would be in a gathering and a man would not even ask his companion [about a matter], for the question and its answer would both be present with him — due to what God has favored upon us through you. However, sometimes a matter comes to us about which nothing has come from you nor from your forefathers. So we look to the best of what is present with us and the most compatible of things with what has come to us from you, and we take by it.'
He said: 'Far be it! Far be it! By God, whoever perished, perished by that, O Ibn Hakim!' He then said: 'May God curse Abu Hanifa! He used to say, "Ali said, and I say."'
Muhammad ibn Hakim said to Hisham ibn al-Hakam: 'By God! I only intended that he grant me permission regarding qiyas (analogical reasoning).'

key_terms.الْقِيَاسِ: Analogical reasoning (qiyas) — the practice of deriving rulings for new issues by analogy with established cases. Central to Sunni jurisprudence (especially Hanafi) but rejected in Shia fiqh.
key_terms.فُقِّهْنَا: You granted us understanding (fiqh) in religion — the narrator acknowledges the Imam as the source of religious knowledge
key_terms.هَلَكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ: Whoever perished, perished — referring to those who used personal opinion and qiyas in place of authentic Imam narrations
key_terms.هَيْهَاتَ: Far be it! — a strong exclamation of rejection and disavowal

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kazim say about qiyas (analogical reasoning) in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) emphatically condemns the practice of qiyas (analogical reasoning in jurisprudence) when applied to religious law. Muhammad ibn Hakim, a companion who practiced ijtihad using qiyas, approached the Imam hoping to get his approval, but instead received a sharp condemnation. The Imam warned that the use of personal opinion and analogy led to the destruction of earlier Muslims, and cursed Abu Hanifa — the founder of the Hanafi school — for his well-known reliance on qiyas and personal opinion over the narrations of Imam Ali (AS). This hadith is central to the Shia rejection of analogical reasoning as a source of Islamic law, emphasizing exclusive reliance on the Imams' teachings.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Hakeym who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! We (acquired) understanding in the Religion and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Made us needless of the people by you<sup>asws</sup> to the extent that if the group from us happens to be in the gathering, a man does not ask our companions a question but he is (already) prepared for its answering - based upon what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Favoured upon us through you<sup>asws</sup>.  However, sometimes the thing (a matter) is referred to us for whom nothing has come with regards to it from you<sup>asws</sup>, nor your<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup>, anything. So we look at the best of that which hold us (from you<sup>asws</sup>) and we prepare the most satisfactory of the things of what has come to us from you<sup>asws</sup>. So we take with it’ (issue a Fatwa accordingly).

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Far be it! Far be it! In that, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, was destroyed the one who were destroyed, O Ibn Hakeem!’ Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse Abu Haneefa. He was saying, ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> said, and I say (my words supersede his<sup>asws</sup> - nouzobillah )’.

Muhammad Bin Hakeem (the narrator) said to Hisham Bin Al Hakam (a narrator), ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I did not intend except that he<sup>asws</sup> should allow me regarding ‘الْقِيَاسِ’ the analogising’ (giving Fatwas based on Qiyas).
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn Hukaym who has said the following.

“I asked (Imam) abul Hassan Musa (a.s.), ‘May Allah take my soul in your service, “Please make us Faqih, people of proper understanding in religion. Allah has granted us the blessing of your existence among us and has made us independent of other people. This blessing is so great that even if a whole group of us would come to one place no one would need to ask an other come up with a question so that the other would prepare and answer for it. Sometimes we come across an issue for which we have heard nothing from you or from your forefathers. We than look into the best of the resources with us and the closest that we have with us from you can we take such a finding as an authority? “

Never, never, by Allah O ibn Hakim many people have been destroyed in it” Reply from the Imam (a.s.). Ibn Hakim has said that the Imam then said, “May Allah. Abu Hanifah who used to say, “Ali said so and so, therefore, I said so and so.”
Muhammad ibn Hakim has said that he told Hisham ibn al-Hakam, “By Allah, I only wanted the Imam to give us permission to use analogy.’”
